inputs.declared_question: How can a gathering reveal shared structure without making consensus the measure of truth?

internal_region.title: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs

sources_checked.title: Polis: Scaling Deliberation by Mapping High Dimensional Opinion Spaces

source_facts.claim: The Computational Democracy Project continues to describe Polis as an open-source, real-time system for gathering, analyzing, and understanding what large groups think in their own words using statistics and machine learning.

The official Polis page continues to describe participant-authored short statements, agree, disagree, or pass responses, semi-random presentation, adaptive participation, and participant-created survey dimensions.
The maintained public repository continues to describe Polis as open-source AI for large-scale open-ended feedback and remains licensed under AGPL-3.0 with additional permission.

FN-25 continues to imagine a larger gathering process that carries testimony, evidence, art, forecasts, values, and institutional histories, and may preserve disagreement rather than end in consensus.
source_facts.locator: Field Note 25: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs

cartographer.inference: The existing possible shared inquiry remains accurate. Polis makes large-scale participant feedback and opinion structure legible, while FN-25 imagines a wider artifact of evidence, values, provenance, ratification, and explicit dissent. No new external node or edge is needed to restate that distinction.
cartographer.uncertainty: The selected public sources do not resolve how facilitation, moderation, identity, and data governance should transfer into a Cyberdelic gathering. Those questions remain open rather than being inferred from technical proximity.
cartographer.attribution: External facts are attributed to the Computational Democracy Project, its public Polis repository, and the publisher-hosted methods paper. Internal continuity is attributed to the exact FN-S0-001 publication.
cartographer.stop_reason: The oldest external neighbour was rechecked as one bounded inquiry. Its evidence and limits remain coherent, so the Cartographer stopped without expanding to other deliberation systems.

Do not change proposal lifecycle, rotate Attending, or publish a dated tending page. The current Community Notes arrangement remains recent and no Polis dormancy signal is present.
Leave relationships.json unchanged. The recheck refreshed confidence in a proposal but did not create a ratification event.

librarian.decision_reason: These three supported phrases improve discovery for people seeking a large-group feedback process without adding a new object, changing the relation, or ranking the project by attention.

How can a gathering reveal shared structure without making consensus the measure of truth?
